newsitem.title: FRANCE: New Bank of France team leaves rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: New Bank of France team leaves rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bank of France held its key intervention rate unchanged Thursday in what some saw as a sign the independent central bank was sticking to its cautious policy despite the appointment of two new members.

The central bank, whose nine-member monetary policy council held its first meeting since Pierre Guillen and Jean-Rene Bernard joined the body this month, said it was leaving its intervention rate at 3.15 percent.
Economists had said the new composition of the council could have tipped the balance in favour of faster interest rate cuts. But they said Thursday they still expected monetary easing soon.

"I'd say it's a fairly cautious approach, in part designed to quash speculation the two new council members would instantly advocate looser monetary policy," Sonja Gibbs, bond strategist at Nomura International, said.
"It doesn't change expectations at all for rate cuts in the first quarter of at least 10 to 15 basis points," she added. A basis point is one-hundreth of a percentage point.

The bank has traditionally maintained a small premium over Germany's repo rate, now at 3 percent, to cushion the franc against attack on currency markets and to defend its link to the mark, seen as the cornerstone of the European single currency project.
The intervention rate was last cut -- from 3.20 percent -- on Dec. 17.
